rules.title: Repository Pattern
rules.check: Business logic MUST use repository/data interfaces, NOT DbContext directly.

rules.title: Async Data Access
rules.check: All data I/O MUST be async.

rules.title: No Tracking for Read-Only
rules.bad_example: var users = await _context.Users.ToListAsync(); // Tracks changes overhead

rules.title: Explicit Loading
rules.check: Lazy loading is FORBIDDEN. Use explicit .Include().
rules.bad_example:
// Lazy loading enabled globally
var orders = user.Orders; // N+1 Risk

rules.title: Projection Queries
rules.check: Fetch only needed columns using .Select(), NOT full entities.
rules.bad_example:
var user = await _context.Users.FirstAsync(u => u.Id == 1);
return user.Name; // Loaded all columns uselessly

rules.title: Transaction Scope
rules.check: Multi-step mutations MUST use explicit transactions.

rules.title: Optimistic Concurrency
rules.check: Entities with concurrent access MUST have concurrency tokens (e.g., RowVersion).
rules.good_example:
// Throws DbUpdateConcurrencyException if changed
_context.Entry(user).Property(p => p.RowVersion).OriginalValue = version;

rules.title: Query Timeout
rules.check: All database queries MUST have timeouts configured.
rules.bad_example:
// Default timeout might be infinite
await cmd.ExecuteNonQueryAsync();

rules.title: Connection Resilience
rules.check: Enable Retry Policies (Resiliency) for transient failures.

rules.title: Index Awareness
rules.check: Queries on large tables MUST use indexed columns.
rules.bad_example:
// 'Bio' is nvarchar(max) and unindexed
var u = await _users.FirstAsync(u => u.Bio.Contains("Admin"));
rules.good_example:
// 'Email' is indexed
var u = await _users.FirstAsync(u => u.Email == "admin@corp.com");

rules.title: Bulk Operations
rules.check: Batch inserts/updates MUST use bulk methods for operations exceeding 100 records.

rules.title: Soft Delete Pattern
rules.check: Soft deletes MUST use global query filters. Direct deletion of soft-delete entities is forbidden.

rules.title: Audit Columns
rules.check: Entities MUST have audit columns (CreatedAt, UpdatedAt, CreatedBy) populated automatically.

rules.title: Connection Pool Sizing
rules.check: Connection pool size MUST be explicitly configured based on expected concurrency.
rules.bad_example:
// Default pool size may be too small for high-traffic apps
var conn = "Server=db;Database=app;";

rules.title: DTO Record Types
rules.check: DTOs MUST be immutable records with required properties or primary constructors.
rules.rationale: Records provide value equality, immutability, and concise syntax. Required properties ensure complete initialization.

rules.title: DTO Organization in Contracts
rules.check: DTOs MUST be organized in Dto/ folder with subdirectories by category.
rules.bad_example:
Domain.Contracts/
├── UserDto.cs
├── OrderDto.cs
├── PageDto.cs
├── MediaDto.cs
├── UserValidator.cs
└── OrderValidator.cs
rules.good_example:
Domain.Contracts/
├── Dto/
│   ├── Core/
│   │   └── BaseDto.cs
│   ├── Users/
│   │   ├── UserDto.cs
│   │   └── UserProfileDto.cs
│   ├── Orders/
│   │   ├── OrderDto.cs
│   │   └── OrderLineDto.cs
│   ├── Content/
│   │   ├── PageDto.cs
│   │   └── MediaDto.cs
│   └── Enums/
│       └── OrderStatus.cs
└── Validators/
    ├── UserDtoValidator.cs
    └── OrderDtoValidator.cs

rules.title: Generic Response Wrapper
rules.check: List endpoints SHOULD use a generic response wrapper with items and total count.
rules.bad_example:
// Inconsistent return types
public async Task<List<UserDto>> GetUsersAsync() => ...
public async Task<UserDto[]> GetOrdersAsync() => ...
public async Task<IEnumerable<PageDto>> GetPagesAsync() => ...
rules.rationale: Consistent response structure enables client-side pagination handling and generic UI components.
